taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-26, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 17.9 | 13.68 | 13.68
2 | 50.4 | 5.82 | 19.50
3 | 514.6 | 0.68 | 20.18
4 | 502.0 | 17.67 | 37.85
5 | 194.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AKQ-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-26, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-26 in survey area T exhibits a five-layer resistivity profile. The sequence begins with 17.9 ohm-m at the surface, rising to 50.4 ohm-m and 514.6 ohm-m in layers two and three. The resistivity then declines through layer four (502.0 ohm-m) and layer five (194.4 ohm-m). 

Applying the curve-type notation rules:
- Layers 1-2-3 (17.9 < 50.4 < 514.6) result in A.
- Layers 2-3-4 (50.4 < 514.6 > 502.0) result in K.
- Layers 3-4-5 (514.6 > 502.0 > 194.4) result in Q.

The resulting AKQ curve matches the classification currently recorded in the survey files.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKQ", "label_issue_flagged": false}
